recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core reconciliation. If the work group wants to revisit Group on current DeviceUsage.subject, change the OO Incubator source and explicitly account for FHIR-41413 rather than editing inactive core resource files.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive R5 issue requesting removal of Group from DeviceUseStatement.subject because known use cases did not justify Group, while explicitly allowing possible later reintroduction if clear use cases emerged.
initial_application: Core commit dd762a0d5230470982fdf5f7bfa8b9e00dfa1a14 applied the issue by deleting the Group targetProfile from source/deviceusestatement/structuredefinition-DeviceUseStatement.xml. DeviceUseStatement was later carried forward as DeviceUsage, with source/fhir.ini retaining an old-to-new mapping.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini omits DeviceUsage and DeviceUseStatement from the active core resource list, and source/device-module.html links DeviceUsage to the OO Incubator IG. FHIR-41413, later Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6, reintroduced Group for DeviceUsage.subject for family/household care and is already represented on the combined branch by an external-repo audit commit. The current OO Incubator DeviceUsage JSON has Patient and Group targets plus the family/household comment.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit and made no core source edits. Removing Group from the inactive core DeviceUsage XML would be out of build scope and would contradict the later FHIR-41413 decision that governs the current external artifact.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied/Persuasive with Modification OO decision reintroduced Group for DeviceUsage.subject for family/household care and now controls the current external artifact; it already has a combined-branch audit commit.
